Subject: Checkoutly - sudden p95/token lag at 06:45 PT

Attached: prod_metrics_20291101.png and a qlog export. No config changes on our side. Can you confirm whether this is on Redwood's routing or a model-serving bottleneck? We're seeing impacts in checkout flows for ~12% of requests.

Alice Wong

From: soojin_lee@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Fwd: Checkoutly - sudden p95/token lag at 06:45 PT — triage update

Quick triage notes (what we can confirm so far):
- Routing: no large-scale routing policy flip. No new model variant launches in the relevant region.
- Runtime: observed transient worker GC spikes and high kernel latency on a subset of pods from 06:42–06:58 PT. Those pods showed low KV cache hit rates (cache miss surge ~4x).
- Queue behavior: queue depth increased because a subset of requests could not warm KV cache (prefixs) fast enough; continuous batching held requests waiting for KV reads.
- Resources: GPU utilization on the impacted host pool was normal-ish; CPU scheduling/GC and disk I/O for KV read subsystems peaked.

Immediate mitigation applied (10:30–10:50):
- Hotfix: increased allowed burst capacity for Checkoutly's org by +20% on the serving pool to shift some traffic to spare capacity.
- Cache priming: triggered a targeted KV-warmup job on the affected model version for active prefixes (low risk).

Impact: These reduced observed p95 in the pool back to ~1.3x baseline in our quick check. We still see occasional token emission stalls on a small percentage of requests — likely due to late-arriving cold KV reads.

Product asks / short-term roadmap asks (for prioritization):
1) Persistent prefix cache: current cache falls back too aggressively after churn — request we fast-track a persistent prefix caching option (config per-customer) to reduce warmup penalty.
2) Enhanced cache prefetch during scale events: an automatic prefetch trigger based on queue depth metric.
3) Route-level emergency throttle: allow customer-level soft-throttles at the router so we can shed lower-priority requests without capacity commits.

Ben, can you confirm whether any routing fallback code paths still exist that might be reclassifying requests into a slower execution plan?
Action items:
- Soojin: continue monitoring; I'll keep the burst-cap increases active for 2h unless product prefers otherwise.
- Ben: routing audit + logs by 13:00 PT.
- Marissa/Karthik: propose a customer message.

Soojin Lee
SRE, Redwood Inference
(Attachments: qlog_snapshot_1101.tar.gz; prod_metrics_20291101.png)

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: ops@checkoutly.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, soojin_lee@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2029-11-01T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Checkoutly - quick update and next steps (ETA + mitigation)

Alice —

Thanks for flagging this. Short update from our side after triage: between 06:40–07:00 PT a subset of serving workers experienced sustained cache miss storms and GC events which led to request queuing and elevated p95. We pushed three mitigations and next steps below.

What we did (already active):
- Opened temporary burst capacity for Checkoutly to shift 20% of traffic to healthy workers.
- Ran a targeted KV-warmup on the impacted model version for your active prefixes.
- Increased routing retry window to reduce requeue churn for requests in-flight.

Immediate customer impact: we reduced p95 to ~1.3x baseline; edge cases remain for ~2–3% of requests (short token emission stalls).

What we're doing next (timeline):
- Next 60 minutes: Soojin will continue monitoring and will alert if we see regression.
- Next 24–72 hours: Engineering (product + runtime) will evaluate a fast-follow to enable a persistent prefix cache and an automatic prefetch trigger for scale events. We will provide prioritization and timeline within 48 hours.

Operational ask for Checkoutly: can you share a short list of top-25 prefixes (or top request patterns) used in peak flows? That will help our warmup job and reduce tail risk.

Commitment: we will send a 1-hour check-in or sooner if anything changes. If the issue regresses, we will coordinate an immediate bridge and provide a post-incident summary within 72 hours.

Draft customer-facing content above — please let us know if you'd like any changes before I hit send.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Customer Success, Redwood Inference
